claims.statement: Step Law v3 reports non-power-of-two widths, including 960 and 1280.

locators.locator: Table 4; released dense CSV h column

scope.evaluation: Published configuration table

claims.limitations: These configurations establish permissibility, not optimal aspect ratio or hardware throughput.

claims.statement: The pinned Step Law fitting release contains 1911 dense and 708 MoE observation rows.

scope.evaluation: Row count and grouped observed minima

claims.limitations: Observation counts are not the paper headline experiment count or proof of independent full runs.

claims.statement: Released Step Law bs values count sequences; the 2048-token context must be applied before comparison with token-batch laws.

locators.locator: Section 3.2; release seq_len and bs columns

scope.evaluation: Batch-unit conversion

claims.limitations: Do not assume another tokenizer/context or release uses this conversion.

claims.statement: Step Law v3 fits LR and token batch jointly as conditional power laws in its declared parameter and token units.

scope.model: Paper dense baseline with tested transfers
scope.evaluation: Final losses used to locate HP optima

claims.limitations: Coefficients are recipe-conditional; neither width-only muP nor an unqualified recurrent-MoE prescription.

claims.statement: For constant actual group LR, the nominal AdamW normalized decay timescale is token_batch / (LR * decay * horizon_tokens).

scope.evaluation: Shrinkage accounting

claims.limitations: This formula is an accounting relation; an empirically optimal timescale need not remain constant across size or horizon. MuonH norm constraints are different.

claims.statement: Width transfer requires the complete parameterization, initialization and per-parameter update convention; fixed-depth width evidence is not depth-transfer evidence.

locators.locator: Tensor Programs V width-transfer construction; AI2 fixed-family ladders

scope.evaluation: Transfer conditioned on unchanged conventions

claims.limitations: No universal per-group LR multiplier is inferred for a different optimizer or recurrent architecture.

claims.statement: The pinned Marin normalizer uses xxh3_128 of normalized UTF-8 text for a 32-hex-character content ID.

scope.evaluation: Content identity and join contract

claims.limitations: The upstream record ID and registry source identity remain separate provenance fields.

claims.statement: PR 8303 reports a 292-source row-alignment census and a bucket pass over 18710478349 documents.

locators.locator: PR description: census and bucket production pass

scope.evaluation: ID/row alignment and calibrated bucket outputs

claims.limitations: Author-reported production counters. We did not scan the cloud corpus or independently time the pass.

comparison.uncertainty: No independent census or timing uncertainty established here

claims.statement: The current token-only reference scorer and historical fusion/content-type bucketing are different compatible-input contracts.

scope.evaluation: Input compatibility and calibrated bucket assignment

claims.limitations: Per-type calibration cannot be substituted into the token-only caller without a content type; downloading a scorer path does not establish access.

claims.statement: Historical Harrier and the newer Luxical reference DAG use different embedding bases; equal bucket numbers do not imply equal content.

locators.locator: Historical report embedding section; current reference_pipeline.py

scope.evaluation: Taxonomy compatibility

claims.limitations: Weights cannot be ported by cell number without a taxonomy mapping or new mixture search.

claims.statement: The legacy Harrier HF export has 116 experiment rows: 72 fresh_full and 44 resumed_cooldown.

scope.evaluation: Public record/schema/simplex audit

claims.limitations: Not training text; resumed branches are not independent full runs. Different registry generations have different counts.

claims.statement: The inspected hero JSON has three phase vectors over 200 cells and satisfies the eight-epoch cumulative cap under the documented target budgets.

scope.evaluation: Simplex, positivity and cumulative exposure accounting

claims.limitations: Availability values are published metadata, not independently measured unique-token supply; this does not establish deployment of planned phases.

claims.statement: Issue 9126 reports final d1536 macro BPB 0.91844, 0.72% lower than the older ladder, with 15/16 subsets improving.

scope.optimizer: Recipe linked in issue; not independently qualified
scope.evaluation: Paloma 16-subset final macro BPB

claims.limitations: Reported final, not our rerun. 1.20x is a fitted compute equivalent assuming equal throughput; no final-rung confidence interval retrieved.

comparison.baseline: Old mixture ladder in Marin issue8435
comparison.protocol: Completed d1536 final16-subset Paloma macro; recipe differences remain in source
comparison.uncertainty: No final-rung confidence interval retrieved; compute-equivalent speedup assumes equal throughput

claims.statement: The June context-extension experiment changes 65536 to 262144 context for 1000 updates at sequence batch 256 while controlling checkpoint and recipe.

locators.locator: Launch contract and pinned context-extension launcher

scope.evaluation: 250-update cadence; long-context capability outcomes require separate scores

claims.limitations: A TPU v4-2048 run; not a directly qualified 96-H100 recipe or proof of the winning long-document skew.

claims.statement: Captured discussions report completed 2x and 4x long-document treatments; the captured 8x discussion establishes launch, not a final winner.

scope.data: Same base store with length skew
scope.evaluation: Reported completion versus launch, not comparative outcome

claims.limitations: Status as captured 2026-11-04. We did not retrieve private checkpoint bytes or a complete paired final benchmark table.

claims.statement: PR 7250 reports a 64-H100 eight-step native Grug SFT smoke ending at loss0.712 and a saved checkpoint.

locators.locator: PR description: end-to-end validation and geometry

scope.evaluation: Reported training loss, save success and memory fit

claims.limitations: A systems smoke, not a completed SFT benchmark or demonstrated optimum. The target geometry uses AdamH because the considered Muon workspace did not fit.

comparison.baseline: Native step42150 base checkpoint initialization; no scored benchmark comparator
comparison.protocol: 8-step64-H100 infrastructure smoke, training loss and save
comparison.uncertainty: One reported smoke; no final SFT task score

claims.statement: The RSI Snowball example reports improved synthesized-family probes alongside lower Smartie pool validation score.

scope.evaluation: 214 probes and300 Smartie tasks; paired task bootstrap

claims.limitations: Author-reported task means with four attempts/task. The probe gain does not establish broad-task improvement; held-out family definitions matter.

comparison.protocol: 4attempts/task;214synthesized-family probes and300Smartie tasks; paired task bootstrap

claims.statement: A fixed-TPP log-linear design cannot independently identify intercept, size exponent and token-horizon exponent.

scope.horizon: Fixed D/N ray versus crossed grid
scope.evaluation: Design-matrix rank

claims.limitations: Exact rank argument for this log-linear model; a more constrained model may identify fewer quantities.

claims.statement: Doubling batch and applying the exact decay-only compensation preserves total constant-LR shrinkage in the analytical fixture.

scope.model: One decayed scalar weight with zero gradient
scope.evaluation: Exact shrinkage equality to floating-point tolerance

claims.limitations: This is not an optimizer-training comparison and does not transfer AdamW rules to MuonH.

claims.statement: The fixture yields pooled token NLL2.5 and equal-subset macro NLL2.0 for the same supplied loss sums.

scope.evaluation: Token-pooled versus equal-subset macro

claims.limitations: Synthetic data. Real BPB requires consistent raw bytes, masks, tokenizer and context; task macro cannot be equated to corpus-pool BPB.

claims.statement: Reusing weights changes executed visits and attention work without duplicating the stored weight matrices.

locators.locator: Explicit illustrative matrix counter in kb_workbench.compute

scope.evaluation: Stored matrices versus routed matrix visits and attention FLOPs

claims.limitations: Matrix-only count excludes norms/biases/nonlinearities. Routing can visit different experts; executed work is not a unique-active-parameter count.

measurements.unit: matrix parameters; norms and biases excluded

claims.statement: The current all-in planning ledger allocates 576 prehero and2304 hero GPU-days within96 GPUs times30days.

scope.evaluation: GPU-day accounting; not measured throughput

claims.limitations: A resource proposal. H100 SKU/topology, measured throughput, data supply and trainer qualification remain unresolved.

questions.question: What model and token horizon can96H100GPUs support in30days?
questions.gaps: Need GPU SKU/topology, measured useful throughput, qualified trainer/recurrence and serving constraints.

questions.question: How do unique retained tokens, repeated exposures and phase weights determine feasible data demand?
questions.gaps: Need accessible prepared sources and a real retained-token/loader census under the chosen tokenizer.

questions.question: How do we reproduce Marin topic/quality buckets rather than only its search records?
questions.gaps: Need historical compatible embeddings/scorer/calibration/store access, or declare a newly rebuilt taxonomy.

questions.question: What does width-transfer evidence establish about width, depth and expert choices?
questions.gaps: Need matched shape experiments and target-hardware throughput; no optimal depth/expert count is established for our target.

questions.question: How should we tune LR, token batch, decay and schedule before fitting transfer laws?
questions.gaps: Need resolved group conventions and actual proxy grid/repeat/holdout training observations.

questions.question: What experiment grid makes size/horizon laws identifiable and tests extrapolation?
Which evaluation contracts make checkpoints and training stages comparable?
Which Marin long-context experiments were configured/completed and what winner is actually established?
questions.gaps: Need complete paired per-length final capability outcomes; captured8xlaunch alone supplies no winning-skew conclusion.

questions.question: What SFT/RL evidence establishes systems readiness versus broad capability gains?
questions.gaps: Need complete post-training runs and independent capability/guardrail evaluations for the chosen target.

questions.gaps: Need selected cyber sources, quality/contamination fixtures, held-out tasks/families and matched training controls.
